global_issues.title: Non-Sagittal (Side-View) Angle Detected
global_issues.message: The video was recorded from a frontal, angled, or non-sagittal perspective. In Starting Strength (Ref p. 2 Fig 2-1 & Ref p. 8 Fig 2-5), squat depth, bar-path verticality, and back inclination are strictly defined in the sagittal plane. In a frontal projection, depth cannot be validated because the femur is foreshortened. Camera must be positioned 90 degrees directly to the side of the lifter at hip height.
global_issues.actionable_cue: Relocate camera to a pure side-view perpendicular to the lifter's stance at hip height.

supporting_evidence.standard_benchmark: The apex of the crease of the shorts (Point B) must drop clearly below the top of the patella (Point A) so the femoral plane breaks parallel with the floor.

findings.explanation: Cannot assess sagittal planar biomechanics from a frontal or off-angle view. Plane between hip crease and patella cannot be resolved.

findings.uncertainty_and_limitations: Camera perspective violation prevents planar measurement.

non_assessable_side_view_criteria.source_section: Generating hip drive & Learning to Squat
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.standard_description: Heels should be approximately shoulder-width apart. Excessively wide stance limits depth; narrow stance jams thighs against gut.
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.why_unassessable: Stance width is a coronal-plane measurement. A 2D side-view camera collapses the lateral axis. Verify by recording a frontal or rear view.

non_assessable_side_view_criteria.standard_description: Toes should point outward at approximately 30 degrees to align femurs and adductor origin/insertion angles.
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.why_unassessable: Transverse-plane rotational angle. Side-view perspective cannot resolve 30° rotation of the foot sole. Check by looking down at feet during setup.

non_assessable_side_view_criteria.criterion_name: Knees Shoved Out / Valgus Collapse Prevention
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.standard_description: Knees must be actively shoved outward to track parallel with feet, preventing medial knee valgus collapse.
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.why_unassessable: Lateral knee tracking occurs in the frontal plane. From the side, the near leg occludes the far leg and lateral knee cave is invisible. Record a front-view set to assess knee tracking.

non_assessable_side_view_criteria.criterion_name: Grip Width & Wrist Alignment (Thumbs on Top, Straight Wrists)
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.standard_description: Thumbs placed on top of bar, wrists straight with forearms to keep bar weight on back rather than loading wrists.
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.why_unassessable: Hands and wrists are occluded by 450mm bumper plates and shoulders in a 90° side view. Check grip in the rack before unracking.

non_assessable_side_view_criteria.standard_description: Bar should be racked at mid-sternum height so lifter does not have to tiptoe to unrack or rerack.
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.why_unassessable: Requires clear view of empty rack hooks relative to lifter sternum before unrack.

narrative_only_exclusions.topic: Front Squat vs Back Squat Mechanics Comparison
narrative_only_exclusions.reason_excluded: Theoretical narrative explaining why vertical front squat requires high quadriceps force. Not an evaluation standard for a barbell back squat.

narrative_only_exclusions.topic: Quadriceps vs Hamstrings Muscle Recruitment Claims
narrative_only_exclusions.reason_excluded: Anatomical/EMG narrative commentary. Muscle activation cannot be measured by computer vision without surface electromyography sensors.

narrative_only_exclusions.topic: Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Shearing Force Claims
narrative_only_exclusions.reason_excluded: Orthopedic biomechanics explanation of force cancellation. Theoretical explanation, not an assessable video rule.
Physiological description of the stretch-shortening cycle. Explains turnaround velocity, but not a pass/fail geometric rule.
